chunks: We have enjoined on man to be good to his parents; but if they try to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, then do not obey them. To Us is your return, so We will inform you of what you used to do.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if parents command their child to commit shirk?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this verse establishes the hierarchy of obedience, prioritizing Tawhid (monotheism) over parental authority, a principle exemplified by Imam Ali (AS) who balanced filial piety with unwavering adherence to divine command. The term 'husnan' (goodness) is interpreted broadly to include material care and emotional kindness, provided it does not compromise core beliefs, while 'jahada' implies a persistent, active effort by parents to induce shirk. This creates a nuanced legal framework where disobedience is limited strictly to the specific act of shirk, preserving the general duty of birr (kindness) towards parents.
